svg.text: D2. What a slice holds, now that ice is a biome
Three arenas from the same planet to the same scale (153,600 units): an ordinary one, one through both poles, one that clips a cap.
An ordinary slice (no ice): 2 cities, 4 towns, 4 biomes, 77% land, 0% ice (0% sheet, 0% sea ice)
Through both poles: 3 cities, 5 towns, 6 biomes, 60% land, 23% ice (15% sheet, 8% sea ice)
Clipping a polar cap: 3 cities, 3 towns, 5 biomes, 57% land, 23% ice (15% sheet, 8% sea ice)

What ice does to the picker
How often a random circle carries ice (at least 8% of its length)
A circle through both poles meets the minimum (2 cities, 3 towns, 3 biomes, half land)
The same circle meets a relaxed minimum (1 city, 2 towns, 3 biomes, 40% land)
Touch-downs where the picker finds a slice meeting the minimum (the earlier planet: 92%)
Accepted arenas that carry at least 8% ice
Rules that change: ice sheet and sea ice count as biomes (so a polar slice easily has its three); sea ice is not land (half of the length must still
be land, ice sheet included); cities and towns stay out of the caps, so a slice through a cap has less room for them.
The picker itself does not change: it still tries the circles through the touch-down and a city and keeps the first that meets the minimum. Ice only
changes which circles pass.
